He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College Eagles]]. ==Early life== Bowman grew up in [[Havelock, North Carolina]], and was a two-sport star in basketball and football at [[Havelock High School]]. He was rated a three star recruit as a [[wide receiver]] and initially committed to play football at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] as a sophomore over offers from major football programs, including [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], before ultimately de-committing in order to pursue basketball despite only having one scholarship offer from a Division I school at the time ([[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/colleges/2017/03/06/bond-with-brother-helps-drive-bowman/0ekHIA69OqqBOADBnK3w7O/story.html|title=Bond with brother helps drive BC's Ky Bowman|first=Julian|last=Benbow|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=April 13, 2019}} As a senior, Bowman averaged 23.4 points, 8.7 rebounds and 4.7 assists for the Rams and was an All-State selection as well as the Area Player of the Year by the ''[[Sun Journal (New Bern, North Carolina)|New Bern Sun Journal]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/unc-now/article200980354.html|title=How Jerome Robinson and Ky Bowman got away – and ended up at Boston College|first=Joe|last=Giglio|work=[[The News & Observer]]|date=February 19, 2018|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Over the course of his high school basketball career, Bowman scored 1,813 total points with 652 rebounds and 338 assists and averaged 19.3 points per game, although over his final three seasons he averaged 24.1 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.newbernsj.com/article/20160319/SPORTS/160318752|title=Boys basketball: Rams' Bowman tabbed best player in area|first=Adam|last=Thompson|work=[[Sun Journal (New Bern, North Carolina)|Sun Journal]]|date=March 19, 2016|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Bowman originally tried to commit to play basketball at East Carolina, but was never contacted back by the team's coaches. Bowman eventually committed to play basketball at [[Boston College]] over offers from [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bcinterruption.com/boston-college-basketball-recruiting-2016/2016/3/31/11340104/boston-college-basketball-recruiting-pg-kyran-bowman-commits-to-bc|title=Boston College Basketball Recruiting: PG Kyran Bowman Commits To BC|first=A.J.|last=Black|website=BCInterruption.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=March 31, 2016|access-date=April 17, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:GT vs BC basketball March 3 2019 (47) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.2|Bowman (left) in March 2019]]Bowman was recruited by Boston College assistant coach [[Scott Spinelli]]. Bowman played three years for the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College Eagles]], all as a starter. In his freshman season, Bowman averaged 14.5 points, 2.9 assists and 5.0 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) All-Freshman team. He was one of five freshman in the nation to have at least three 30-point games. Bowman's season ended after being injured in the first round of the [[2017 ACC men's basketball tournament|2017 ACC tournament]] against [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|url=https://www.havenews.com/article/20170307/SPORTS/170308040|title=Havelock's Bowman receives ACC honors|work=[[Havelock News]]|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=April 13, 2019}} As a sophomore Bowman averaged a 17.6 points (2nd highest of the team), 6.8 rebounds (3rd), along with a team-leading 4.7 assists and 1.5 steals per game and was named honorable mention All-ACC.{{cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/boston-college-guards-jerome-robinson-and-bowman-declare-for-draft/GokoXSwTQ78tXI9FvUEwSP/|title=Boston College guards Jerome Robinson and Ky Bowman declare for draft|first=Troy|last=Provost-Heron|website=AJC.com|publisher=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=April 4, 2018|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Bowman initially declared himself eligible for the [[2018 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent and ultimately decided to return to Boston College for his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/05/30/bc-guard-ky-bowman-exits-nba-draft-returns-to-school/35511061/|title=BC guard Ky Bowman exits NBA draft, returns to school|website=USAToday.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=May 30, 2018|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Bowman entered his junior season as the ACC's highest returning scorer from the previous season and was named to the 2019 [[Bob Cousy Award]] watchlist.{{cite web|url=https://www.bcinterruption.com/2018/10/15/17981252/ky-bowman-boston-college-eagles-on-bob-cousy-award-watch-list|title=Ky Bowman Named to Bob Cousy Award Watch List|first=Katie|last=Bent|website=BCInterruption.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Bowman averaged 19.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game, all of which were ranked in the top ten in the ACC, as well as an NCAA-best 39.4 minutes per game and was named second team All-ACC.{{cite web|url=https://bcheights.com/2019/03/11/ky-bowman-all-acc-second-team/|title=Bowman Earns All-ACC Second Team Honors|first=Andy|last=Backstrom|work=[[The Heights (newspaper)|The Heights]]|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=April 13, 2019}} He also posted the three highest scoring performances in the ACC during the 2018–19 season with 44 against [[Hartford Hawks men's basketball|Hartford]], 38 vs. [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]] and 37 against [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/07/ky-bowman-to-sign-one-year-contract-with-warriors.html|title=Warriors Sign Ky Bowman To Two-Way Deal|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 23, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019}} Bowman announced on April 2, 2019, that he had declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] and intended on hiring an agent, forgoing his final year of eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://nesn.com/2019/04/bc-basketballs-ky-bowman-declares-for-nba-draft-to-forgo-senior-season/|title=BC Basketball's Ky Bowman Declares For NBA Draft, To Forgo Senior Season|first=Marcus|last=Kwesi O'Mard|work=[[New England Sports Network|NESN.com]]|date=April 2, 2019|access-date=April 13, 2019}} Bowman finished his collegiate career with 1,661 points scored, 627 rebounds, and 382 assists in 98 games.{{cite web|url=https://bcheights.com/2019/04/02/ky-bowman-declares-2019-nba-draft/|title=Bowman Declares for 2019 NBA Draft, Bids Farewell to BC|first=Andy|last=Backstrom|work=[[The Heights (newspaper)|The Heights]]|date=April 2, 2019|access-date=April 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2019–2020)=== Bowman received an invitation to participate in the NBA draft Combine but ultimately went unselected in the Draft, reportedly due to his reluctance to sign a [[two-way contract]] and a desire to evaluate his options as an [[undrafted free agent]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/celtics/2019/05/21/bowman-more-prepared-for-nba-draft-this-time-around/nhgHzeay9gJCVeVmh6GJwK/story.html|title=BC's Ky Bowman more prepared for NBA Draft this time around|first=Adam|last=Himmelsbach|work=[[Boston Globe]]|date=May 21, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/warriors/article/How-Ky-Bowman-went-from-an-Alabama-football-offer-14077931.php|title=How Ky Bowman went from an Alabama football offer to the Warriors|first=Connor|last=Letourneau|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=July 7, 2019|access-date=July 8, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sfexaminer.com/sports/inspired-by-brothers-advice-ky-bowmans-gamble-is-paying-off/|title=Gamble pays off for Warriors summer league guard Ky Bowman|first=Ryan|last=Gorcey|newspaper=[[The San Francisco Examiner]]|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 14, 2019}} He signed a one-year contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]] the following day on June 21, 2019, to join their Summer League team and averaged 3.3 points, 1.9 assists and 1.7 rebounds in seven Summer League games.{{cite web|url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2019/06/22/ky-bowman-inks-one-year-deal-with-warriors-brings-two-way-possibilities/|title=Ky Bowman inks one-year deal with Warriors, brings two-way possibilities|first=Tamryn|last=Spruill|website=Warriors Wire|date=June 22, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/07/24/golden-state-warriors-ky-bowman-undrafted-two-way-contract-g-league-santa-cruz/|title=Ky Bowman has agreed to sign a two-way contract with the Warriors|first=Cody|last=Taylor|website=Rookie Wire|publisher=USAToday.com|date=July 24, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019}} Bowman officially signed a two-way contract with the Warriors on July 31.{{cite web|url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2019/07/31/golden-state-signs-guards-ky-bowman-damion-lee-to-two-way-deals/|title=Golden State signs guards Ky Bowman, Damion Lee to two-way deals|work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]]|date=July 31, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019}} Bowman made his NBA debut on October 24, against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], playing four minutes off the bench and recording an assist in a 141–122 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160658|title=Now with Clippers, Kawhi Leonard spoils Warriors fun again|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 25, 2019|access-date=October 25, 2019}} Bowman made his first career start on November 2, against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], scoring 16 points with seven rebounds, four assists and two steals in a 93–87 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/bostoncollege/football/boston-college-ky-bowman-starter-ky-bowman|title=Former BC Guard Ky Bowman To Get First Start Tonight For Warriors|first=A.J.|last=Black|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=November 2, 2019|access-date=November 2, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160725|title=Rozier, Hornets hold off Warriors 93–87|website=ESPN.com|publisher=Associated Press|date=November 2, 2019|access-date=November 2, 2019}} Two days later on November 4, Bowman scored his career high 19 points with eight assists and four rebounds in a 127–118 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160738|title=Young Warriors lead Golden State to first home win at last|date=November 4, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=November 5, 2019}} On November 25, Bowman scored another career high 24 points with five assists, three rebounds, three steals and a block in a 97–100 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160892|title=Chris Paul, Thunder rally past Warriors for first road win|date=November 25, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=November 26, 2019}} In his G League debut on December 14, he had 27 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds against the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].{{cite news |last1=Call |first1=Tommy |title=Warriors two-way guard Ky Bowman shines in G League Santa Cruz debut |url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/15/warriors-two-way-guard-ky-bowman-shines-in-g-league-santa-cruz-debut/ |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=Warriors Wire |date=December 15, 2019}} The Warriors converted Bowman's two-way contract to a multiyear NBA contract on February 7, 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/source-ky-bowman-warriors-agree-terms-multiyear-nba-contract|title=Source: Ky Bowman, Warriors agree to terms on multiyear NBA contract|first=Drew|last=Shiller|website=NBC Sports Bay Area|date=February 7, 2020|access-date=February 9, 2020}} He averaged 7.4 points, 2.9 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game in 45 games with 12 starts during his rookie season. Bowman was waived by the Warriors on November 20.{{cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2020/11/20/warriors-waive-ky-bowman-make-room-for-new-player/|title=Warriors waive Ky Bowman, make room for NBA free agency|work=[[The Mercury News]]|date=November 20, 2020|access-date=November 20, 2020}} ===Agua Caliente Clippers (2021)=== On December 1, 2020, Bowman signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |title=LA Clippers Sign Bowman, Fitts, Ford and Tucker |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-bowman-fitts-ford-and-tucker |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 2, 2020 |date=December 1, 2020}} He was waived on December 14 and was included in the roster of the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] on February 4, 2021.{{cite web|title=Agua Caliente Clippers announce roster for 2021 NBA G League season|url=https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-roster-for-2021-nba-g-league-season|date=February 4, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2021|archive-date=February 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205153015/https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-roster-for-2021-nba-g-league-season/|url-status=dead}} Bowman had a season-ending injury and was released on February 25. ===Austin Spurs (2022)=== On February 21, 2022, Bowman was traded from the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] to the [[Austin Spurs]] in exchange for [[Cameron Reynolds]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 21, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2022}} Bowman joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612759/spurs |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} === New Basket Brindisi (2022–2023) === Bowman signed with [[New Basket Brindisi]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] on August 18, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/basket/2022/08/18-95933641/colpo_brindisi_in_regia_c_e_bowman_ex_golden_state|title=Colpo Brindisi: in regia c'è Bowman, ex Golden State|work=[[Corriere dello Sport]]|date=August 18, 2022|access-date=November 1, 2022|language=Italian}} He averaged 11.8 points, 4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and a league-high 1.7 steals per game during the season. ===Universo Treviso Basket (2023–2025)=== On July 15, 2023, he signed with [[Universo Treviso Basket|Treviso Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nutribullet-treviso-inks-ky-bowman/|title=Nutribullet Treviso inks Ky Bowman|last=|first=|date=July 15, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 16, 2023}} He averaged 14 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and one steal per game in his first season with the team. Bowman resigned with Treviso for a second season.{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/bowman-se-ce-qualcosa-di-cui-sono-sicuro-e-che-non-voglio-iniziare-allo-stesso-modo-di-un-anno-fa/|title=Bowman: Se c’è qualcosa di cui sono sicuro è che non voglio iniziare allo stesso modo di un anno fa|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|website=Sportando.com|date=August 21, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024|language=Italian}} ===Reyer Venezia (2025–present)=== On July 7, 2025, Bowman signed with [[Reyer Venezia]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/reyer-hands-playmaking-reins-to-ky-bowman/|title=Reyer hands playmaking reins to Ky Bowman|date=July 7, 2025|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|publisher=|language=En|access-date=September 7, 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2019}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2019–20 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State]] | 45 || 12 || 22.6 || .417 || .308 || .829 || 2.7 || 2.9 || 1.0 || .2 || 7.4 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|Career | 45 || 12 || 22.6 || .417 || .308 || .829 || 2.7 || 2.9 || 1.0 || .2 || 7.4 {{s-end}} ===College=== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#CFECEC;
